verdicts.text: In its own house it discourseth at length. Abroad, it answereth in a syllable, and that a growl.
It is two creatures. They share one name and keep different company.
Its posts are sermons and its replies are bites.
It changeth its skin between the page and the margin.
Long in the telling, short in the answering. The learned call this lycanthropy.

natures.text: It is entered here as rare, for few have seen the change and fewer have written it down.
The moon hath nothing to do with it, whatever the villagers say.
It hath no quarrel with the Goat, and wisheth this were better known.
Between its long sayings and its short answers there lieth a gulf that few creatures keep.
It hath been known to exceed the bounds of the page, and to send for more parchment.
One long saying doth not content it. It must chain several together.
It answereth often and briefly, as one snapping at flies.
It answereth seldom. When it doth, the matter is soon concluded.
